title: Huawei convicted of trade secret theft and bank fraud in US
h1: A US jury convicts Huawei of conspiring to steal trade secrets and bank fraud, but clears it of racketeering
description: A federal jury in New York convicted Huawei on November 24, 2026 of trade secret conspiracy and bank fraud while acquitting it of racketeering conspiracy.
standfirst: Jurors rejected the government's most sweeping charge, a racketeering conspiracy, after a trial of more than two months. Huawei says it will appeal the counts it lost.
keywords: Huawei verdict, Huawei convicted, Huawei trade secrets, Huawei bank fraud, Huawei racketeering acquitted, Huawei trial New York
takeaways: The jury returned its verdict on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, after a trial that lasted more than two months.
Huawei and three affiliates faced 12 charges; the racketeering conspiracy count was rejected.
Huawei's lawyer said the company will appeal the convictions.
body: A federal jury in New York found Chinese telecommunications company Huawei Technologies guilty on Tuesday, November 24, 2026, of conspiring to steal trade secrets and of bank fraud, the Associated Press reported. The same jury acquitted the company of the most serious charge in the case, a racketeering conspiracy, which prosecutors had used to describe Huawei as an enterprise that took intellectual property from US companies.

Huawei and three affiliated companies faced 12 charges, including racketeering conspiracy, bank fraud, wire fraud, sanctions violations, and conspiracies to steal trade secrets and obstruct justice, Al Jazeera reported. Prosecutors called more than 60 witnesses over the trial of more than two months; the defense called 15.

The government said Huawei took technology from competitors and partners, did business in sanctioned countries including Iran and North Korea, and gave false statements to US officials and banks to hide it. Court records list Cisco Systems, Motorola Solutions, T-Mobile, Quintel USA and Fujitsu among the companies prosecutors described as victims, according to the AP.

Defense lawyers argued that a few isolated cases of misconduct among Huawei's more than 200,000 employees had been stitched into a conspiracy that never existed. Outside court, Huawei attorney Brian Heberlig said the company would appeal and called the racketeering acquittal a vindication, telling reporters that the verdict "repudiated the central government narrative in the case," the AP reported.

It grew out of the December 2018 detention in Canada of Meng Wanzhou, Huawei's chief financial officer and the founder's daughter, on a US warrant tied to the company's business in Iran. She later reached a deferred prosecution agreement and returned to China in 2021, and the charges against her were dropped. Prosecutors added the trade secret allegations against the company in 2020.

The AP said it is unclear how the verdict will affect Huawei's business. The company has been barred for years from selling equipment to US carriers and has been shut out by allies including Canada and Britain, but it sells phones and network gear worldwide and its chips have become an important alternative in China to those from companies such as Nvidia. Neither report gave a sentencing date.

faq.q: Was Huawei found guilty of racketeering?
faq.a: No. On November 24, 2026 the jury acquitted Huawei of racketeering conspiracy but convicted it of conspiring to steal trade secrets and of bank fraud.
